text:
anu: Heads-up: onboarding run for nova-70b-int4v2 shows strange token repeat exactly at 16384/16385 boundary when KV caching is enabled. Samples look like '...and then he said said said'.
tom: Can you share the exact run command and kernel flags you used?
anu: Repro command: 
```bash
./serve_test --model nova-70b-int4v2 --mode longprefill --kv-cache=on --seq-len=32768 --kernel int4_fast --prompt data/long_story.txt
```
dray: I tried same but with --kernel fp16_safe and no repeats. So likely kernel-specific. Did you record compiler metadata?
anu: Compiler metadata: rope_cap=65536, rope_scale=0.9992. Runtime prints rope_scale=1.0008 for int4_fast path. Also saw kv_index wrap at 16384 in debug logs.
mira: Any quantization parameter diffs? int4 rounding/scale?
anu: int4 scales identical between builds. The pattern suggests index arithmetic drift, not quant per se.
tom: Could be stride calc using 32-bit signed accumulators overflowing at that offset + some stride. If stride uses token_index * multiplier in fixed point, it could drift.
dray: I added logging to kernel shim to emit (token_idx, kv_idx, rot_phase_fp) for tokens 16360..16396. Dump attached to canary logs.
qa-bot: buildbot: Canary with extra logs deployed to canary-07 (cid: c7d9).
mira: I scanned the csv: kv_idx increments correctly until token 16384 then jumps by +2 every 64 tokens thereafter on int4_fast. fp16_safe stays linear.
tom: +2 every 64 tokens — weird. That periodicity smells like a 6-bit mask somewhere (64) combined with a truncation. Maybe an intermediate uses uint8 or int16 and a multiply shifting sequence modulo 256/65536.
anu: I instrumented the host-side prefill that computes base_index and stride and found that base_index remains correct, but kernel-side computed kv_idx differs. That points to kernel arithmetic.
dray: Quick mitigation idea: add runtime check for seq_len > 16000 to force kernel fallback (fp16_safe) until kernel fix is in. That's low-risk but will impact int4 perf for long sequences.
mira: Create a temporary gating feature flag 'int4_longseq_fallback' and flip it on for the canary.
qa-bot: test-runner: scheduled full goldset regression (100 prompts longprefill) against canary-07 and master.
anu: Results: master (int4_fast) shows mean repeat ratio 0.18 at boundary; canary with fallback shows 0.01. Perplexity delta across goldset before/after fallback: +0.2 (acceptable).
tom: Root cause hypothesis: fixed-point rotation multiplier computed as (pos * inv_rope_scale) then cast to int32 for lookup; for int4 kernel we were using a 32-bit accumulator but a downstream shift used 16-bit intermediate in asm. Overflow causes wrapped indices at that periodicity.
dray: I submitted a kernel patch that widens intermediate to 64-bit and forces normalized mod ops. PR: https://git.internal/r/nn/krnl/patch/4821
qa-bot: ci: PR 4821 passed unit tests but failed longprefill smoke on gitlab-runner-3 (timeout).
mira: I reran smoke locally, patch fixes the KV drift in my run. We should land after CI flakes are resolved.
anu: Created onboarding hold ticket RW-13001, flagged 'blocked' until patch lands. Also added an integration test to runner that exercises int4 kernels with seq-len 16384..33000.
tom: After patch lands, we should run a quantitative eval vs fp16 baseline: sample KL divergence, repeat-rate, and PPL slides at windows [0..16384], [16384..32768].
dray: Agreed. I'll add the metrics to the eval harness and run overnight.
qa-bot: ci: PR 4821 re-run passed full pipeline.
mira: Merged and enabled feature flag toggle off on canary. Re-running full goldset now.
anu: Goldset looks clean. No boundary repeats. Perf penalty due to fallback is 6% but temporary.
tom: Nice work. Add postmortem note, and let's add a pre-merge bot check that runs the longseq integration for any kernel-level change.
anu: Done — ticket RW-13004 for pre-merge gating. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
